newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Wednesday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by more than adequate hog supplies and waning packer demand going into the Independence Day holiday on Friday, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 lower at $60.00 to $60.50 in the country and $61.00 to $61.50, but could slip further as the day progresses, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at plants. Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.50-$60.00/country and $60.00-$61.00/plants.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.50 to $60.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants, dealers there said.
"There's plenty of hogs and no one's killing on Friday or Saturday," an Indiana hog dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants, buyers said.
Hog runs swelled Tuesday amid moderating temperatures and lower humidity in the Corn Belt, talk that cash hog prices were near a peak and knowledge that packer demand would be slow Thursday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota marketings Tuesday were 112,000 head, well above the 105,000-head estimate, USDA said.
